text:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool pool-eu-3 experiencing sustained enqueue > 120s for 3 mins, auto-scale not catching up (scale events delayed). Possible thundering burst from 2 customers. Paging oncall.
sam: oncall here. I see errors in the queue metrics + elevated 5xxs on the routing proxy. Linking dashboard: https://console.redwood.example/d/pool-eu-3?from=now-15m
meera: looking. Autoscaler logs show scale_attempts queued, but Cloud-agent rate limited creation by quota: "quota_exceeded: GPU instance create rate" around 2060001205. That explains delay.
jordan: confirmed. Two tenants spiking — cust-A (batch job) and cust-B (bot traffic). cust-A has sudden vector-ingest traffic. cust-B is high qps on short-ttl requests. We should protect production surface.
sam: mitigation options: 1) toggle burst_capacity on pool-eu-3 (instant, uses reserved burst capacity), 2) manually bump max_instances for pool, 3) apply temporary per-tenant quota/rate-limit, 4) disable nonessential features (async reranks) for Dedicated until stabilized. Thoughts?
meera: on-call suggestion: enable burst_capacity first (fastest), then if still high, apply rate limits to cust-B and throttle cust-A ingestion. I can flip burst and bump max_instances if needed.
tom: FYI support is getting tickets from cust-B complaining about slowness. I'll add a note to customers: "We're mitigating an infrastructure surge; you may see brief latencies." Want me to message both?
sam: go ahead, please. minimal details: we are applying emergency scaling changes.
meera: preparing toggle command. Using infra CLI: this will enable burst mode and set a short cooldown for autoscaler.
meera: running:
```
redwoodctl dedicated pools update --pool-id=pool-eu-3 --set burst_capacity=enabled --set autoscale.max_instances=30 --set autoscale.cooldown=60s
```
meera: CLI returned: "queued change -> applying to control plane". Agent reported 3 burst units available.
jordan: control-plane shows instance delta +6 in progress. Proxy 502 rate dropping.
sam: Pls monitor latencies and enqueue. If queue drops <30s and 5xxs recede, keep burst enabled for 10min and then reassess.
meera: also applying tenant throttles for cust-B to protect others.
meera: command:
```
redwoodctl quotas update --tenant cust-B --requests-per-second=20 --burst=50 --reason "emergency rate limit to stabilize pool-eu-3"
```
meera: rate limit applied. telemetry shows cust-B qps down from 650 -> 22 within 15s.
jordan: nice. cust-A ingestion still high but running on burst instances now. Enqueue for cust-A down from 140s -> 18s.
tom: I've posted status to customers: "We've enabled temporary scaling and rate limiting to stabilize performance; tracking closely." :thumbsup:
liz: any risk to billed capacity for these customers? Will they see sudden overage charges?
meera: burst uses reserved burst pool tied to customer contract for Dedicated. For cust-A and cust-B they're on standard Dedicated plans; we won't bill unexpected cloud bursts immediately, finance will reconcile in the weekly report. If we keep burst more than 6 hours, we'll need approval.
sam: timeline and next steps: keep burst on and throttles for 15 minutes; if stable, start rolling burst down and re-evaluate. If unstable, escalate to exec oncall for capacity increase or customer-specific mitigations.
jordan: agree. Setting an alert to auto-disable burst after 15m unless we extend:
```
redwoodctl alerts create --name "auto-disable-burst-pool-eu-3" --expr "time() - burst_enabled_ts > 900" --action "redwoodctl dedicated pools update --pool-id=pool-eu-3 --set burst_capacity=disabled"
```
meera: added. Also added a temporary runbook note in the incident channel with commands used.
sam: handoff in 10m to jordan. Current state: burst enabled, autoscale bumped to max 30, cust-B throttled, cust-A running ingestion on burst. Latency and 5xxs improving. Customer impact: degraded latencies for ~10m for cust-B only, other tenants protected. No data loss.
jordan: taking over in 10. Will watch metrics and coordinate rollback. If things look green for 12m, plan to reduce max_instances to 20 then disable burst.
tom: I'll keep customers updated every 15m. Any message template? I used: "We've applied temporary rate limits and enabled emergency scaling — you may see slightly elevated latencies while we stabilize. No action required on your side."
sam: good.
(meera): after 8 minutes: queue median <12s, 5xxs at baseline. Autoscaler created 5 instances, all healthy.
(jordan): taking over now. Sam, leaving note: I will monitor for 30 mins and then hand back to oncall rota.
sam: thanks. final: please file a post-incident note with root cause = cloud instance create quota throttle + noisy tenants; action items = (1) request higher create-rate quota from cloud for EU region, (2) add per-tenant burst gating to avoid single tenant exhausting burst, (3) add synthetic that simulates burst to validate autoscaler handles high-fanout. Tagging meera and jordan.
jordan: will create the ticket. Closing this thread here but will update after 30m.
oncall-bot: Incident (pool-eu-3-surge) -> assigned to jordan; status: monitoring; bridge: https://zoom.incident/12345

[jordan later update]: 2060001299: 30m passed, metrics stable. Disabled burst and scaled max_instances back to 18 with:
```
redwoodctl dedicated pools update --pool-id=pool-eu-3 --set burst_capacity=disabled --set autoscale.max_instances=18
```
[jordan]: cust-A and cust-B back to baseline. Closing incident. Follow-ups: ticket #INF-472 for quota request, #INF-473 for per-tenant gating, and postmortem scheduled tomorrow 09:30 UTC."
